findings.finding_text: emit_and_exit interpolates stalenessAlarm.stampPath into the JSON log line RAW (no json_escape) — unlike indexedHeadSha/cliInstalled/cliExpected/detail; sed capture truncation at I1's backslash-escaped quotes leaves a dangling backslash and the raw interpolation can swallow the closing quote, producing an unparseable line while the wrapper exits 0
findings.label: HIGH
findings.rationale: json_escape around the interpolation — same pattern as the neighboring fields; also strips control chars, closing EH-006's TAB/CR variant

findings.finding_text: stampPath control characters (TAB/CR) pass the sed [^"]* extractor and land raw inside the JSON line — parseCycleLine rejects unescaped control chars, poisoning the whole cycle record
findings.label: LOW

findings.finding_text: QDS_GITNEXUS_HOME split-brain: wrapper pins lock dir + stamp reads + I1 reader to the override home, but the default canonical reindex hardcodes <repoRoot>/.gitnexus (install-gitnexus-plus.sh:509-515) — with only the home overridden, crossCheck fails every cycle naming crossCheck, not the real cause

findings.rationale: Split-brain guard: QDS_GITNEXUS_HOME set non-empty while REINDEX_CMD is still the production default → pre-cycle FATAL exit 3 naming both vars and the writer's hardcoded target (fixtures always override the reindex command, so the suite path stays open). Header env-table clarification + suite prose fix at :196-199 + new fixture test

findings.finding_text: crontab.factory ships no PATH; Debian cron PATH=/usr/bin:/bin excludes bun's install locations, so every tick exit-3s pre-cycle; /var/log/qds may not exist and a failed redirect kills the entry before the wrapper runs — the entire observable output silently absent
findings.label: MED
findings.rationale: Wrapper gains documented bun-location fallback resolution (command -v bun → $HOME/.bun/bin, /usr/local/bin, $HOME/.local/bin → export PATH) mirroring the canonical script's gitnexus fallback idiom; crontab header comment names the PATH prerequisite and the one-time operator creation of /var/log/qds; suite source-pin asserts the fallback lines exist

findings.finding_text: PATH prerequisite documented only in the wrapper header one hop from the file the operator installs; first fired tick likely FATALs until operator hand-edits crontab
findings.label: LOW
findings.rationale: Covered by the EH-001 fix (wrapper fallback + crontab header comment)

findings.finding_text: Both AC5 lock fixtures synchronize via a fixed 2s sleep inside the holder while tick B must complete bash boot + git rev-parse + bun staleness spawn inside that window — under CI load B arrives after release and the coalesce proof flakes
findings.label: MED
findings.rationale: Determinize: holder holds ≥30s; B's skip line is polled with a bounded waitFor; the holder is killed (SIGTERM) only after B's refusal is observed — no fixed sleep gates any assertion

findings.finding_text: num_or_null rejects JSON exponential notation — JSON.stringify emits e.g. 2.77e-7 for |ageHours| < 1e-6 (stamp within ±3.6ms of the reading clock), silently coercing a measured age to null on a fresh verdict
findings.label: LOW
findings.rationale: Regex accepts optional [eE][-+]?[0-9]+ exponent + comment citing the producer (JSON.stringify). No deterministic end-to-end test exists (the window is ~3.6ms wide and drive-through-the-real-wrapper timing cannot reliably hit it) — documented in the comment per the house measured-not-assumed idiom

findings.finding_text: exec 9>> without close-on-exec: reindex/contract children inherit fd 9 sharing the open-file description — a selective wrapper kill leaves the lock held by an orphaned cycle that never writes its line; the header's 'kernel releases on ANY exit' claim is inaccurate while children live
findings.label: LOW
findings.rationale: Invoke both children with 9>&- (bash -c "$CMD" 9>&- </dev/null) so the lock's only holder is the wrapper itself and the header claim becomes true; header comment updated; suite source-pin asserts the redirection on both invocation lines

findings.finding_text: emit path's date leg is bare under set -e — a transient date(1) failure aborts emit after reindex+contract succeeded, losing the record the adjacent code explicitly hardened the clock for
findings.label: LOW
findings.rationale: Harden: now=$(date ... || true); if empty fall back to $CYCLE (tick-start UTC — skew beats a lost record); comment explains the degradation

findings.finding_text: flock error vs refusal conflated: every non-zero flock -n exit records skipped-overlapping exit 0 — a broken lock (ENOLCK-class) degrades to silent never-refresh with healthy-looking skip lines
findings.label: LOW
findings.rationale: Portable flock cannot distinguish (exit 1 covers both; no -E on macOS brew flock — measured). Honest fix is truth in docs: header + inline comment state the conflation and its observability signature (recurring skip lines with rising stalenessAlarm = broken lock, not contention); behavior unchanged
